model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)
model_label: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (run on the component engine: revenue x Core FFO margin, less non-revenue-generating (recurring) capex = AFFO; discounted at the USD cost of equity with net debt held at ZERO because Core FFO is already after net interest expense)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 (Dec-25 year) total revenues, US$m, ESS_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (10-K FY2025 XBRL). Revenue is the DRIVER line only; the flow valued is AFFO = Core FFO less non-revenue-generating capital expenditures. FY2025 Core FFO margin on revenue was 56.3% (1,062.740 / 1,887.345); non-revenue-generating capex was 6.6% of revenue (124.318 / 1,887.345); AFFO margin 49.7%.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares used in the FFO calculation for FY2026 guidance (66,525 thousand; Q2 2026 supplemental page S-15, 8-K filed 2026-07-29). This count INCLUDES the ~2.2m Operating Partnership common units because the numerator (Core FFO attributable to common stockholders AND unitholders) is stated before the OP-unit noncontrolling interest. Common shares outstanding alone were 64,279,012 at 30-Jun-2026 (10-Q). Held FLAT: FY2026 YTD buybacks of $61.9m (254,001 shares, 0.4% of the count) are already in the 66.525m guidance count; SBC is expensed inside G&A within Core FFO, so projecting further dilution would double count. Q2 2026 actual diluted count was 66,462,974.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow discounted is AFFO derived from Core FFO, which is struck AFTER consolidated net interest expense ($65.6m in Q2 2026 alone). Deducting balance-sheet net debt on top would charge the financing twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never capitalise a post-interest flow and then subtract net debt). total_debt and cash below are recorded for audit and leverage context only.
inputs.total_debt_note: US$m at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q via XBRL, ESS_Metrics.csv TotalDebt): unsecured notes, mortgage notes payable, lines of credit and term loans. After the balance-sheet date, on 24-Sep-2026 the OP entered a new $275m unsecured term loan at SOFR + 0.80% (8-K filed 2026-09-25, expandable to $500m); its proceeds and use are not yet reported and it does not change the model because net debt is not deducted. Net debt / annualised Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDAre (347.666 x 4 = 1,390.7) = 4.6x on the consolidated figures; the company's own normalised ratio including its pro-rata share of co-investment debt is ~5.4x (Analysis JSON).
inputs.cash_note: US$m cash and cash equivalents at 30-Jun-2026 (10-Q). Working cash only; recorded for audit, not netted.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 AFFO, US$m: Core FFO attributable to common stockholders and unitholders 1,062.740 less trailing-four-quarter non-revenue-generating capital expenditures at 31-Dec-2025 of 124.318 (Q4 2025 supplemental capex page: roof replacements, paving, building and mechanical systems, exterior painting, siding; $2,258 per apartment home on 55,056 average homes) = 938.422, i.e. $14.08 per diluted share on 66.670m FY2025 diluted shares. This is the flow the valuation capitalises. Revenue-generating capex (FY2025 $82.4m; ~$100m guided for FY2026 at pro-rata share -- redevelopment, interior unit-turn renovations, amenities, ADUs) is treated as growth capital funded from retained AFFO and disposition proceeds and is NOT deducted, since the Core FFO growth path already reflects only same-property NOI growth plus modest reinvestment yield; the bear case's higher capex path (to 8% of revenue) is where that judgment is stress-tested. NOT the CSV FreeCashFlow (blank -- SEC XBRL carries no capex for this filer) and NOT operating cash flow (FY2025 $1,074.4m, which is before any capex and after working-capital swings).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 Core FFO attributable to common stockholders and unitholders, US$m ($15.94 per diluted share; Q4 2025 earnings release / supplemental page S-3, 8-K filed 2026-02-04). Nareit FFO was 1,065.136 ($15.98); the Core adjustments (non-core G&A, marketable-securities gains, technology co-investment income, early debt retirement) net to only $2.4m in FY2025. In H1 2026 the gap is large: Total FFO $7.49 vs Core FFO $8.15 per share, because $56.8m of legal settlements (RealPage antitrust ~$36.5m and a separate multi-year dispute ~$19.3m) sit in 'General and administrative and other, net' and are excluded from Core. The model capitalises Core FFO, so these are treated as one-off; if such charges recur they belong in the flows (see key_risks_to_valuation).
inputs.sbc_source: Stock-based compensation ($9.64m FY2025 per Metrics.csv StockBasedComp, ~0.9% of Core FFO) is expensed inside general and administrative expense before net income and is NOT added back in the FFO or Core FFO reconciliations (10-K FY2025 cash-flow statement and supplemental S-3). It is therefore already charged once in the flow being valued; no further deduction is made and house and street bases coincide (SBC-zero convention, REIT row of the routing table).
inputs.interest_income_note: Zero. ESS holds working cash only (net debt ~$6.3bn). Interest income on structured-finance (preferred equity / mezzanine) investments is part of the business model and stays inside Core FFO; the platform is being resized down toward a ~$100m run rate, which is why FY2026 Core FFO guidance carries a -$0.38/share structured-finance headwind.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 buybacks were nil; H1 2026 $61.9m (254,001 shares at $243.76 average) under a new $500m authorisation approved May 2026 with $500m remaining at 30-Jun-2026. Recorded as zero for FY0 (FY2025). Buybacks below NAV are value-accretive but are not modelled as share shrink (see share_count_basis).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:03Z NYSE regular close (Yahoo v8 chart meta); 52-week range 238.46-303.35
inputs.nta_note: GAAP book value per common share: stockholders' equity $5,485.5m / 64.279m common shares = $85.34. Historical-cost book value under real-estate depreciation, NOT a fair-value NTA (US GAAP REITs carry investment property at depreciated cost). Recorded for the P/B sanity check only; it is not a valuation floor. A cap-rate NAV cross-check is more meaningful: annualised Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDAre of $1,390.7m capitalised at 5.0% gives GAV ~$27.8bn, less consolidated net debt $6.33bn = ~$21.5bn or ~$323/diluted share; at a 5.5% cap rate ~$285/share; the current price implies a ~5.7% cap rate on this simple basis (ignores pro-rata co-investment debt and the preferred-equity book, so treat as +/- 5%). The company sold a San Jose JV asset in Q2 2026 at a sub-4.5% cap rate.
inputs.core_ffo_history_source: Q4 earnings releases (8-K exhibit 99.1) for FY2021 (accession 0001140361-22-003634), FY2023 (0001140361-24-005882), FY2025 (0001140361-26-003709) and the Q2 2026 release (0001140361-26-030060); each release restates the prior year alongside.
inputs.ffo_fy2026_guidance: Core FFO $16.03-$16.25 per diluted share (midpoint $16.14, +1.3% on FY2025), $1,066.1-1,081.1m on 66.525m diluted shares; Total FFO $15.37-$15.59 (midpoint $15.48, includes the H1 legal settlements); Q3 2026 Core FFO $3.99. Same-property cash revenue / NOI growth midpoints raised to ~2.7% / 2.8% (GAAP basis 2.9% / 2.9%) on 52,135 same-property homes. Revised 2026-07-29 (Q2 2026 release), midpoint raised $0.20 from the original $15.94.
inputs.recurring_capex_note: Non-revenue-generating capex, trailing four quarters: $124.3m at Dec-2025 ($2,258/home), $111.9m at Jun-2026 ($2,020/home). Q2 2026 quarterly figure $31.2m. Revenue-generating (redevelopment/renovation) capex: $82.4m TTM Dec-2025, $73.0m TTM Jun-2026; FY2026 guidance ~$100m pro rata.
inputs.dividend_note: Annualised common dividend ~$10.36/share (32nd consecutive annual increase, Dividend Aristocrat). FY2025 AFFO payout = 10.36 / 14.08 = 74%; FY2026E AFFO payout on the base-case $14.37 = 72%. Dividend yield at current price 3.8%. Cross-check only; not a model input.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the USD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because AFFO is a post-interest flow and no net debt is deducted. 10-year US Treasury 5.18% (^TNX, 25-Sep-2026 close) + 0.8 beta x 5.5% US equity risk premium = 9.6%, rounded to 9.5%. Beta of 0.8 (below 1.0 and below the 1.2 used for BXP) reflects an A-/Baa1 investment-grade apartment landlord at ~5.4x net debt/EBITDA with 96% financial occupancy, 32 years of dividend growth and no structural demand question comparable to office; it is not lower because the portfolio is concentrated in three tech-exposed West Coast metros and carries California rent-regulation tail risk. The same 9.5% is used in all three scenarios (risk is charged once, in the flows). Cross-check: at current_price the market capitalises FY2026E AFFO/share of ~$14.37 at a 5.3% AFFO yield and FY2026E Core FFO/share of $16.14 at a 5.9% FFO yield, i.e. with 2.5% perpetual growth the price embeds a required equity return of ~7.8%, an equity premium of only ~2.6% over today's 5.2% 10-year -- materially below the house rate. The sensitivity grid shows the current price is reached only at a ~7.5-8.0% cost of equity.
inputs.lease_treatment: ESS's own lessee obligations (ground leases; operating lease liabilities immaterial relative to the $6.4bn debt stack) sit inside property operating expense before Core FFO; not separately modelled and not in total_debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Core FFO 'attributable to common stockholders and unitholders' is stated after the property-level noncontrolling interests (third-party JV partners in consolidated communities: $4.5m of Q2 2026 net income) but BEFORE the Operating Partnership common-unit NCI, which is why the diluted share count used (66.525m) includes the OP units. Unconsolidated co-investments enter Core FFO via equity income plus the add-back of the company's share of their depreciation. No further NCI adjustment is made in the bridge (same convention as BXP/CHC.AX: flows are attributable-only by construction, with the OP units in the denominator).
inputs.notes: Model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity -- routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods SKILL.md REIT row (US equity REIT; GAAP net income swings on gains on sale and remeasurement of co-investments -- FY2024 NI $811.3m / $11.55 EPS vs FY2025 $702.8m / $10.40 vs Q2 2026 $0.97 -- so statutory earnings, P/E and NetMargin are set aside, and the CSV FreeCashFlow column is blank because SEC XBRL carries no capex for this filer). Run on the Drivers/engine route, BXP / GPT.AX / CHC.AX precedent: revenue is the driver line, EBITDA margin row = Core FFO margin (post-interest), D&A = 0 (FFO already adds back real-estate D&A), SBC = 0 (expensed inside G&A within Core FFO), capex row = non-revenue-generating capex as % of revenue, working capital = 0, net_debt = 0, cash_tax_rate = 0 (ESS qualifies as a REIT; the only tax is a small TRS provision already inside Core FFO). First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Price is the 25-Sep-2026 NYSE regular close (last regular session before the 28-Sep valuation date). Balance sheet, debt and share count are from the 30-Jun-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-30), the latest filing; Core FFO, the recurring-capex bridge and FY2026 guidance are from the Q2 2026 and Q4 2025 earnings-release / supplemental exhibits (8-Ks filed 2026-07-29 and 2026-02-04), since ESS.duckdb's core_metrics/kpis tables do not carry FFO/Core FFO/AFFO or recurring capex (XBRL does not tag REIT non-GAAP supplemental metrics) -- these should be backfilled into kpis on a future refresh. The two post-balance-sheet 8-Ks (2026-09-11 conference deck; 2026-09-25 $275m term loan) carry nothing that changes the flows.

historical_growth.eps_basis: Statutory diluted EPS (FY2020 $8.69, FY2022 $6.27, FY2025 $10.40) is dominated by gains on sale of real estate and remeasurement of co-investments ($305.0m of gains excluded from FFO in FY2025, $386.1m in FY2024) and is not used. The 18.4% 3-year figure is a base-year artefact (FY2022 had few gains).
historical_growth.fcf_basis: Core FFO per diluted share (the numerator of the capitalised flow, before the recurring-capex bridge): FY2022 $14.51 -> FY2025 $15.94 = 3.2%/yr; FY2020 $12.82 -> FY2025 $15.94 = 4.5%/yr (the 5-year figure spans the FY2021 COVID trough of $12.49 and the FY2022 rebound). In dollar terms Core FFO grew from $1,038.2m (FY2024) to $1,062.7m (FY2025), +2.4%, on a diluted count that rose 0.2%. AFFO (Core FFO less non-revenue-generating capex) is only reliably reconstructable for FY2025 and TTM Jun-2026 in this session, so the CAGR is on Core FFO/share; recurring capex per home has been broadly stable ($2,020-2,258), so the AFFO series would track it closely. The CSV FreeCashFlow column is blank (no XBRL capex) and is not the basis for anything here.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Core FFO/share 3-year CAGR (3.2%) cross-checked against FY2026 guidance (+1.3% at the midpoint, depressed by a -$0.38/share structured-finance wind-down headwind; +1.8% excluding it) and same-property NOI growth guidance of 2.8%. Revenue growth is the driver line in the engine: the base path starts at 4.0% (H1 2026 revenue +4.2% y/y, reflecting FY2025 acquisitions of $829.4m and same-property revenue +2.7%) and fades to 2.5%. Equity CAGR is NOT used: book value is depreciated historical cost reduced by distributions and buybacks and says nothing about the earning power of a 96%-occupied apartment portfolio.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' equity CAGR (-1.1% 3yr, -1.6% 5yr) diverges from revenue CAGR (+5.5% / +4.8%) by far more than 30%. The divergence is structural for a US GAAP REIT: real-estate depreciation of ~$600m/yr and distributions of ~$670m/yr exceed retained earnings, so book value shrinks while the fair value of the assets and the rental stream both grow. Growth is taken from the Core FFO/share series and guidance instead.
historical_growth.notes: Essex is a mature, slow-compounding landlord: Core FFO/share has grown every year since the FY2021 COVID trough (+16.2%, +3.6%, +3.8%, +2.2%, +1.3%E), with FY2026 the slowest year because the preferred-equity platform is being deliberately shrunk (redemptions of $189.8m in FY2025 and $87.8m in Q2 2026 at 9.6-11.6% yields) and reinvested in wholly-owned communities at lower initial yields. Same-property NOI growth of 2.6-3.8% across FY2025-26 is the underlying engine; management's case for reacceleration rests on supply falling further into 2027 across all three metros and ~6% loss-to-lease in Northern California.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 (4.0% revenue growth) with the Y1 Core FFO margin lands FY2026E Core FFO at ~$1,073.7m = $16.14/share on 66.525m shares, the revised guidance midpoint (H1 2026 revenue was +4.2% y/y on FY2025 acquisitions plus 2.7% same-property growth). Y2-Y4 (3.25-3.5%) reflect same-property revenue growth of ~3% as West Coast supply troughs in 2027 and Northern California's ~6% loss-to-lease burns off, plus renovation/redevelopment reinvestment; SoCal (~40% of NOI) stays 'stable' at 1-2%. Fades to 2.5% (CPI-linked rent growth under California's AB 1482 cap of 5% + CPI on renewals) by Y8.
base.margin_rationale: Core FFO margin (this row is read as Core FFO / revenue, the flow before the recurring-capex bridge) steps down from the FY2025 actual of 56.3% to 54.7% in FY2026 -- the guidance bridge attributes -$0.38/share to the structured-finance wind-down, -$0.09 to G&A/other and -$0.06 to net interest, only partly offset by +$0.60 of NOI growth -- then recovers slowly toward 55.8% as the preferred-equity headwind lapses (the book reaches its ~$100m target run rate) and same-property NOI grows faster than consolidated interest expense (debt is well laddered: ~8% matures 2026, ~6% 2027, ~8% 2028, but rolls from 3-4% coupons into ~5-5.5%). No return to the FY2025 56.3% margin is assumed inside the horizon.
base.capex_rationale: Non-revenue-generating capex held near the observed range (5.7% of revenue on the TTM Jun-2026 figure of $111.9m, 6.6% on the FY2025 figure of $124.3m; $2,020-2,258 per home), drifting up to 6.2% as an ageing 1970s-2000s coastal portfolio absorbs insurance-driven roofing/mechanical and seismic work and California building-code inflation. Gives FY2026E AFFO of ~$956m = ~$14.37/share (a 72% dividend payout on the $10.36 annualised dividend). Revenue-generating capex (~$100m/yr) is treated as growth capital and is not deducted here; the bear case's capex path is where that call is stressed.
base.tax_rationale: Zero: ESS qualifies and elects to be taxed as a REIT and distributes at least 90% of REIT taxable income; the small TRS income-tax provision ($0.1m in Q2 2026) is already inside Core FFO.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% / 2.5% = 14.6x terminal AFFO (a 6.8% terminal AFFO yield) binds below the 18x cap. ESS trades at ~18.9x FY2026E AFFO/share today and coastal apartment REITs averaged ~20-22x AFFO over 2015-2021; the 18x cap is the ceiling for the bull case, not a base-case target.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2026 lands at or above the top of guidance ($16.25) as the Q2 beat pattern continues; AI-driven Bay Area and Seattle hiring follows the office-expansion announcements management cites, Northern California's loss-to-lease burns off in 2-3 years at 5-7% blended rent growth, the 2027 supply trough is followed by a prolonged period of sub-1% deliveries, and disposition proceeds and the $500m buyback authorisation are deployed accretively below NAV. Revenue growth of 4-5% for several years before fading to 3.0%.
bull.margin_rationale: Core FFO margin recovers above the FY2025 level (56.3%) as rent growth of 4-5% falls almost entirely to NOI (fixed property costs, occupancy held at 96%+), Fed cuts through 2027 lower the cost of the 2026-28 maturities, and the structured-finance drag ends by FY2027.
bull.capex_rationale: Recurring capex held at the TTM Jun-2026 intensity (~5.8% of revenue), the low end of the observed range, as capital recycling out of older JV communities lowers the average age of the wholly-owned portfolio.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% / 3.0% = 15.8x, inside the 20x cap. Same 9.5% cost of equity as base: the bull case is better flows and margin recovery, not a cheaper discount rate.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 lands at the low end of guidance as SoCal softness spreads. A West Coast tech-employment downturn (AI-driven headcount efficiency rather than hiring) turns Bay Area and Seattle blended rent growth negative in 2027-28 (as Seattle already was in Q1 2026), occupancy slips toward 95%, and a renewed California rent-control push (a third Costa-Hawkins repeal attempt or expanded local vacancy control) caps renewal growth structurally. Growth troughs at 0.5% before recovering only to 2.0%, below CPI, as regulation binds and the co-investment book is gone.
bear.margin_rationale: Core FFO margin compresses ~5 points as flat-to-negative rent growth meets 3-4% operating-expense inflation (insurance, property tax, labour, tenant-protection compliance), maturing 3-4% coupon debt refinances at 5.5-6%, and recurring legal/regulatory costs of the RealPage kind stop being 'non-core' -- $56.8m of H1 2026 settlements would alone be ~3 points of margin if repeated.
bear.capex_rationale: Recurring capex rises to 8% of revenue: this deducts roughly the FY2025 non-revenue-generating capex plus about a third of the revenue-generating (renovation) capex, on the view that in a weak rental market unit-turn renovations become defensive maintenance rather than yield-generating growth capital, and that insurance-driven wildfire/seismic hardening and climate-related regulation add cost the company would not otherwise have incurred.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% / 1.5% = 12.8x binds below the 15x cap (a 7.8% exit AFFO yield, consistent with where coastal apartment REITs traded in late 2023 when the 10-year last approached 5%).

scenario_narratives.base: Essex delivers the revised FY2026 Core FFO guidance ($16.03-$16.25, midpoint $16.14) with same-property NOI growth of ~2.8%, then reaccelerates modestly as West Coast apartment supply troughs in 2027 and Northern California's ~6% loss-to-lease burns off, while Southern California stays merely stable. Core FFO margin dips in FY2026 on the deliberate wind-down of the preferred-equity book (-$0.38/share) and recovers slowly toward 55.8% as that headwind lapses and NOI outgrows a well-laddered debt stack refinancing from 3-4% to ~5-5.5% coupons. Recurring capex runs at ~6% of revenue, leaving FY2026E AFFO of ~$14.37/share and a 72% payout on the $10.36 dividend. AFFO is capitalised at a 9.5% USD cost of equity with no net-debt deduction and no cap-rate compression assumed; growth fades to 2.5% by year 8 and the terminal multiple is the 14.6x Gordon value, below the 18x cap. At the current price the market capitalises FY2026E AFFO at a 5.3% yield -- a ~7.8% implied cost of equity -- so the base case's shortfall to price is a statement about the required return, not about the operating outlook, which is essentially management's own.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Q2 2026 beat pattern continues and FY2026 lands at the top of guidance; the AI capex cycle turns into Bay Area and Seattle hiring, Northern California blended rent growth runs 5-7% for two to three years while supply stays below 1% of stock after the 2027 trough, and occupancy holds above 96%. Rent growth of 4-5% falls almost entirely to NOI, Fed cuts through 2027 lower the refinancing cost of the 2026-28 maturities, and the structured-finance drag ends by FY2027, lifting the Core FFO margin to 57.5%. Capital recycling below NAV (a JV sale at a sub-4.5% cap rate funding buybacks under the $500m authorisation) adds per-share accretion not modelled in the flat share count. Revenue growth fades to 3.0% and the terminal multiple is 15.8x AFFO, inside the 20x cap -- still below where coastal apartment REITs traded through 2015-2021.
scenario_narratives.bear: Southern California's softness spreads: AI-driven headcount efficiency at large tech employers means Bay Area and Seattle office expansions do not translate into hiring, blended rent growth turns negative in 2027-28, occupancy slips toward 95%, and a renewed statewide rent-control push -- after Props 10, 21 and 33 -- finally caps renewal growth structurally. Operating-expense inflation (insurance, property tax, tenant-protection compliance) of 3-4% against flat rents, refinancing at 5.5-6%, and recurring RealPage-style legal costs compress the Core FFO margin to 51%. Recurring capex rises to 8% of revenue as unit-turn renovations become defensive rather than yield-generating and wildfire/seismic hardening adds cost. Growth troughs at 0.5% and recovers only to 2.0%; exit at a 12.8x AFFO multiple, a 7.8% AFFO yield, roughly where the sector traded when the 10-year last touched 5% in late 2023.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted above the house default (15%) to 25%: the Analysis JSON rates geographic concentration, tech-employment sensitivity and California rent-control risk all 'high', the co-investment wind-down and refinancing at higher coupons are already visible in a FY2026 margin step-down, Southern California (~40% of NOI) is underperforming today, and the 10-year Treasury at 5.2% is a live headwind to both refinancing and the sector's multiple. Base held at the house 50%: the FY2026 guidance has been raised twice, occupancy is 96.3%, the balance sheet is investment-grade with ~5.4x net debt/EBITDA and $1.4bn+ liquidity, and management's outlook (supply trough 2027, NorCal loss-to-lease) is credible and observable. Bull trimmed from the house 35% to 25%: upside is real but bounded -- California's AB 1482 caps renewal increases at 5% + CPI (max 10%), so even a strong market cannot produce the 8-10% rent growth of 2021-22 for long, and a rent surge would itself reignite supply and rent-control politics.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Essex is valued as a stream of AFFO -- Core FFO (already after net interest expense and G&A, excluding gains on sale and one-off legal settlements) less non-revenue-generating capex -- capitalised at a 9.5% USD cost of equity with no net-debt deduction, since the flow is post-interest. Statutory net income (dominated by gains on sale and co-investment remeasurement -- FY2024 EPS $11.55 vs FY2025 $10.40 vs Q2 2026 $0.97) and the CSV free-cash-flow column (blank, because SEC XBRL carries no capex for this filer) are both set aside. The base case is essentially management's own FY2026 guidance with a modest post-2027 reacceleration, fading to CPI-like 2.5% growth; risk is charged once, in the flows, with the same discount rate in all three scenarios. The result is that the current price is not supported at a 9.5% required return: the market capitalises FY2026E AFFO at a 5.3% yield, i.e. a ~7.8% implied cost of equity, which is a 2.6% equity premium over a 5.2% 10-year Treasury. Two cross-checks sit either side of the model: a cap-rate NAV of ~$285-323/share (5.5-5.0% cap on annualised Adjusted EBITDAre, consolidated net debt only) is above the price, while the AFFO model at the house rate is well below it. The gap between them is the gap between private-market cap rates of 4.5-5.5% and a 9.5% public cost of equity; this model deliberately does not close it by lowering the rate. Depreciated-cost book value ($85.34/share) is recorded for the P/B sanity check only.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: this is the single largest swing factor. Every 50bp on the 9.5% cost of equity moves the base value by roughly 7-8%, and the current price is only reached at ~7.5-8.0%. If the 10-year falls back toward 4%, the same beta and ERP give ~8.5% and a materially higher value.

Core FFO vs Total FFO: $56.8m of H1 2026 legal settlements (RealPage antitrust, a separate multi-year dispute) are excluded from the Core FFO the model capitalises. If algorithmic-pricing and tenant litigation becomes a recurring cost of doing business in California, it belongs in the flows -- the bear margin path is where that is charged.

Recurring-capex definition: the base case deducts only non-revenue-generating capex (~6% of revenue) and treats ~$100m/yr of renovation/redevelopment capex as growth capital. If that capital is really needed just to hold rents in a 1970s-2000s coastal portfolio, AFFO is ~$1.50/share lower than modelled (the bear case's 8% capex path).

California rent regulation: Costa-Hawkins repeal has been rejected three times at the ballot (2018, 2020, 2024) but each attempt cost the industry tens of millions and the margin of defeat narrowed; a successful measure or expanded local vacancy control would cap growth structurally below the 2.5% terminal rate.

Geographic and tenant concentration: ~100% of NOI in three West Coast metros with tech-sector-linked demand; Southern California (~40% of NOI) is already lagging, and AI-driven headcount efficiency could keep Bay Area/Seattle hiring below what office-expansion announcements suggest.

Revenue is the driver line, not the valued flow: the FY2026 margin step-down comes from the preferred-equity wind-down and interest, not from the properties; a faster or slower wind-down, or refinancing at higher coupons than the ~5-5.5% assumed, moves the outcome without any change in revenue growth.

Share count: 66.525m includes OP units and is held flat; buybacks below NAV under the $500m authorisation would be accretive and are not modelled, while any equity issuance to fund acquisitions above the cost of capital is likewise not modelled.
